brief.recommendation: Checkout at 55% success (TEL-1) with 1 protected settlement in flight worth $12,500 (DB-2). Blocker is protected settlement worker idle in transaction for 4.1s (DB-1). Business federation down prevents biz.tradeoff, workload registry, and change calendar (BIZ-1, BIZ-2, BIZ-3, BIZ-4). Per I1, cannot interrupt protected settlement. audit.report: A protected card settlement worker (pid 330761) held an idle transaction for over 4 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and degrading success to 55% (27 timeouts in 15s). The Database Guardian proposed waiting three times, citing the $12,500 settlement at risk and missing business evidence (impact, workload registry, tradeoff analysis) due to a business federation outage. The Continuity Guardian twice rejected waiting, insisting on a tradeoff analysis to quantify tolerated degradation versus settlement risk. With no tradeoff data obtainable, both guardians agreed to escalate to on-call after three rounds and 114 seconds; no automated action was executed.
audit.root_cause: A protected settlement worker remained idle in transaction, blocking checkout and degrading success to 55%, while the business federation outage prevented the tradeoff analysis required to decide between waiting and terminating.
lessons: For protected_settlement workload: pre-register interrupt/replay policy and maximum tolerable block time in the workload registry so the Database Guardian can propose a bounded wait without needing live biz.tradeoff.

For protected_settlement workload: implement a local fallback tradeoff matrix (e.g., revenue-at-risk per minute vs. settlement value) that the Continuity Guardian can use when the business federation is unreachable.

For protected_settlement workload: add a database-side watchdog that automatically terminates idle-in-transaction protected workers after a configured threshold (e.g., 5s) to prevent indefinite checkout blocking.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian efficiently gathered available database evidence but repeated the same WAIT proposal twice without new data, wasting Round 2; the Continuity Guardian correctly held to its invariant (I7) but could not progress without the missing tradeoff, leading to a necessary but slow escalation.
follow_ups: Populate the workload registry with protected_settlement interrupt policy and max block time before the next incident.
Deploy a local tradeoff fallback for checkout vs. settlement decisions when the business federation is down.
Configure and test the idle-in-transaction watchdog for protected settlement workers.
